cogs.name: Sensor Bridge
cogs.description: Receives sensor readings from external WeftOS nodes (a Pi 5, an Orange Pi) and writes them into the Seed store, so remote sensing joins the Seed's memory. Readings come from weft-bridge-send; each source gets its own store id. COG-007.

cogs.name: Hardware Catalog
cogs.description: Serves the WeftOS hardware-catalog browse page (Projects -> Modules -> Chips) and the catalog JSON over HTTP, so the appliance offers the catalog on the mesh. Embeds crates/cog-market/catalog/catalog.json and a self-contained viewer; no sensor, no store writes.

cogs.name: Attitude / IMU (HLK-AS201)
cogs.description: Hi-Link HLK-AS201 9/10-axis attitude sensor (3-axis accel + 3-axis gyro + 3-axis magnetometer + barometer; 32-bit DSP) read over a 3.3 V TTL UART at 115200 8N1. Reports orientation (roll/pitch/yaw), acceleration (g), angular rate (deg/s), magnetic field (uT), quaternion, temperature, pressure and height. Protocol CONFIRMED against the Hi-Link AS201 datasheet V1.1 (2025-08-01): FA FB.len.cmd.data.SUM.FC FD framing, cmd 0x00 report with a 42-byte ten-axis payload. The X/Y/Z silkscreen identifies this as an IMU, not a radar.

cogs.name: LD1040C Motion Radar
cogs.description: Hi-Link HLK-LD1040C 10.525 GHz X-band Doppler motion radar on a Cognitum Seed. Senses MOVING targets (micro-motion) within ~3-4 m over a 110 degrees ceiling-mount beam; it does not detect static presence and does not see through walls. The reliable signal is the OUT digital line (HIGH on motion, with the module's 5 s output hold and 2 s re-trigger block), read over a Pi GPIO input. Per window it reports whether motion is currently held, the rising-edge count, the fraction of the window OUT was high, and the seconds since the last motion. The first ~9 s after power-on are a warm-up and are flagged. An optional UART telemetry frame (off by default) best-effort adds the motion amplitude, signal and noise; a field that is not parsed is reported null, never fabricated. A missing OUT line yields a no_source line with null values.

cogs.name: LD2450 Tracking Radar
cogs.description: Reads an HLK-LD2450 24 GHz multi-target tracking radar over a 3.3 V UART (256000 8N1) and reports, per window, the up-to-three targets of the radar's latest frame: x/y in metres in the radar's own frame (not room coordinates), speed in m/s and the distance-gate size, plus the valid-target count, frame rate and parse-error counts. Positions only: no identity, no pose, no bounding box. A missing or silent radar yields null values, never a fabricated reading.

cogs.name: LD6002 Radar
cogs.description: Reads an HLK-LD6002 60 GHz radar over USB-serial UART and reports, per window, the radar's own heart-rate, breathing-rate, distance, target-count and presence-flag outputs, the target positions it streams (x/y metres in the radar's own frame, not room coordinates), plus frame and checksum counts. Values the radar did not report in the window are null. The vitals are the module's on-chip estimates, not medical measurements; no pose, no bounding box.
cogs.sensor_name: Hi-Link HLK-LD6002 60 GHz FMCW vitals radar module

cogs.name: Mentra Live Glasses (companion bridge)
cogs.description: Companion-side bridge that lets a pair of Mentra Live smart glasses join the mesh as a node. The glasses run Android (the MentraOS ASG client) and cannot run a cog themselves, so this cog runs on a companion that can reach them over ADB (USB, or ADB-over-TCP/Wi-Fi) and reports their liveness. Each interval it reads presence (device reachable), battery (level, charging state, plug type, pack temperature and voltage) and link health (ADB round-trip time), emits them as a store vector, and posts a fleet heartbeat so the glasses show up as an online node. Telemetry-first by design; HUD rendering, sensors and audio are built on top of this node once it is joined. Fail-honest: with no ADB or no device it reports no_source and keeps the node offline rather than faking liveness.

cogs.name: Presence Radar (RD-03E)
cogs.description: Ai-Thinker RD-03E 24 GHz FMCW presence + ranging radar (S3KM111L SoC) read over a 3.3 V TTL UART at 256000 8N1. The module streams a 5-byte report frame (AA·dist_lo·dist_hi·state·55) on power-up with no configuration needed. Reports whether a target is present, its distance in cm (±5 cm from 30-350 cm, to ~6 m), the per-minute detection rate and the quiet time since the last detection. Frame layout confirmed by community captures; gesture-code meanings (state 2-8) are vendor-specific and reported raw.

cogs.name: SEN0213 ECG
cogs.description: Reads a DFRobot SEN0213 (AD8232) single-lead ECG through an ADS1115 I2C ADC on the Seed's GPIO header. Exports the raw waveform and a filtered waveform, detects R-peaks (Pan-Tompkins), and reports heart rate, RR intervals, SDNN, RMSSD and a signal-quality score. Flags leads-off, saturation and a flat signal instead of guessing. Not a medical device.

cogs.name: SEN0628 Matrix ToF
cogs.description: Reads a DFRobot SEN0628 8x8 matrix time-of-flight sensor (VL53L7CX + RP2040, 20-3500 mm, 60 deg FOV) over I2C on the Seed's GPIO header. Reports the nearest object and its zone, the valid-zone share, frame-to-frame motion, presence against a learned background, left/middle/right sector distances and per-zone noise, and exports raw depth frames.
cogs.sensor_name: DFRobot SEN0628 8x8 matrix ToF 3D distance sensor

cogs.name: Sensor OTA Push
cogs.description: Pushes an ESP-IDF app image to RuView ESP32 sensor nodes through their authenticated OTA HTTP endpoint (port 8032). Dry run by default: checks the image SHA-256, chip id and app version, reads each node's /ota/status, and prints the upload plan without sending any POST. --apply uploads one node at a time and waits for the node to reboot into the new build. Reaches the ota_0/ota_1 app slots only, never the bootloader, partition table or NVS.

cogs.name: Sound Detector
cogs.description: Detects sound/noise with a KY-038 / LM393 microphone comparator module read through an ADS1115 I2C ADC on the Seed's GPIO header (OUT on A1, so it coexists with the sen0213-ecg cog on A0). Reports whether sound is present, the per-minute event rate, the quiet time since the last event, the activity percentage, level and peak. Tune the module's trimpot (or --threshold) for your room. Works for the common active-high digital OUT and, degraded, for analog-OUT variants.
